title: Canada's Dabrowski, Brazil's Stefani capture Wuhan Open women's doubles title
summary: Canada's Gabriela Dabrowski and Brazilian partner Luisa Stefani captured the women's doubles title Sunday at the Wuhan Open tennis tournament in Wuhan, China.

image.caption: Ottawa's Gabriela Dabrowski, right, and Luisa Stefani of Brazil pose with the trophy after defeating Storm Hunter of Australia and Katerina Siniakova of Czechia 7-5, 6-4 in the women's doubles final at the Wuhan Open on Sunday in Wuhan, China. (Chinatopix Via/China Out/The Associated Press)

blocks.text: Canada's Gabriela Dabrowski and Brazilian partner Luisa Stefani captured the women's doubles title Sunday at the Wuhan Open tennis tournament in Wuhan, China.
Top seeds defeat 3rd-seeded duo of Australia's Hunter, Czechia's Siniakova 7-5, 6-4
The No. 1 seeds defeated the third-seeded team of Australian Storm Hunter and Czech Katerina Siniakova 7-5, 6-4 in the final. Hunter and Siniakova were defending champions.
The win was the sixth of the season for Dabrowski, of Ottawa, and Stefani. They also earned an eighth title as a team and third in a row.
Canada's Dabrowski and Brazilian partner Stefani capture 7th career WTA doubles tournament title
Dabrowski and Stefani also improved their career record to 79-19 and qualified for the season-ending WTA final next month.
Dabrowski captured a 26th career doubles title.
"I'm really pleased with where we are and where our level is," Dabrowski said. "So it's really nice to see it pay off in results consistently throughout the season."

items: Gabriela Dabrowski claims 25th tour-level doubles title of her career at China Open

blocks.text: Dabrowski and Stefan had more aces (five to none) and fewer double faults (three to four) than their opponents. They also registered five breaks in 19 opportunities.
Hunter and Siniakova converted three-of-eight break chances.
Dabrowski and Stefani broke early to build a 4-1 lead in the first set before Hunter and Siniakova rallied to tie the score. The top seeds broke again in the 12th game to take the opening set.
They broke twice in the second set while surrendering their serve once to complete a victory in one hour 32 minutes.
With files from The Canadian Press
